**Analysis summary:**

Both Late Blight reference images I viewed were microscopic (sporangia/sporangiophores), not showing macroscopic leaf symptoms. The Early Blight reference showed widespread leaf browning on a whole plant. The Gray Mold reference was also microscopic.

**Returning to test image characteristics:**
- Large, irregular dark brown to tan necrotic areas concentrated at the leaf tip and one margin
- No concentric ring "target" pattern (argues against classic Early Blight)
- Defined boundary between healthy green tissue and necrotic tissue
- Yellowing/chlorosis transitioning into necrosis
- No visible gray fuzzy sporulation (arguing against Gray Mold)
- No white powdery coating (rules out Powdery Mildew)
- Dry, collapsed texture in affected areas

**Disease reasoning:**
- **Late Blight** (Phytophthora infestans): Produces large irregular dark brown-to-black lesions often starting at leaf margins/tips, with fairly defined boundaries — matches the test image well
- **Early Blight** (Alternaria solani): Would show concentric ring "target" spots with yellow halos — concentric rings absent here
- **Gray Mold** (Botrytis): Usually shows grayish fuzzy sporulation — not visible here
- **Bacterial Canker**: Can cause marginal leaf scorch but typically involves more vascular/systemic symptoms

The large irregular dark brown necrosis at leaf margins and tip, with defined boundaries and yellowing transitions, is most consistent with Late Blight.
